subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should direct new installs from arbitrary npm, git, local, archive, npm-pack, and marketplace sources require explicit provenance acknowledgement while ClawHub, bundled, official-catalog, setup, repair, and update flows remain exempt?
rationale: The implementation now expresses a coherent narrow policy, but adopting a mandatory public CLI consent contract and deciding which executable sources are trusted are maintainer-owned security and compatibility choices.

options.title: Approve the narrowed gate
options.body: Require acknowledgement only for direct new arbitrary-source installs and preserve the documented trusted and internally controlled flows.

options.title: Broaden the gate
options.body: Require acknowledgement in selected setup, repair, or update paths and accept the additional upgrade and automation friction.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Decline the new mandatory acknowledgement until maintainers choose a different provenance or rollout design.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrowed gate
recommendation.body: Require acknowledgement only for direct new arbitrary-source installs and preserve the documented trusted and internally controlled flows.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the strongest merged history for the adjacent ClawHub trust boundary and the proposed narrowed policy.
